scenario: You are building a live network packet intrusion detection system scanning incoming packets against 1,000 malware signatures simultaneously in real-time.
question: Which algorithmic paradigm and data structure should you select for single-pass stream processing?
options: Aho-Corasick Automaton with BFS failure links
KMP repeated sequentially 1,000 times per packet
explanation: Aho-Corasick constructs a Trie with failure transitions in O(m * Sigma), enabling linear single-pass streaming across text in O(n + z) time regardless of the number of patterns.

scenario: A computational biologist needs to detect conserved local motifs between two divergent DNA sequences, discarding non-homologous flanking regions.
question: Which algorithm is mathematically designed for optimal local sequence alignment?
options: Smith-Waterman Algorithm with recurrence clamped at zero
explanation: Smith-Waterman clamps negative cell values to 0 (max(0, ...)), allowing alignment traceback to begin from the highest scoring cell anywhere in the matrix and terminate when 0 is reached.

scenario: You need to sort all suffixes of a 100,000-character genome text to enable fast O(m log n) substring lookups.
question: Which algorithm constructs the suffix array in O(n log² n) or O(n) without building full tree nodes?
explanation: Prefix-doubling sorts suffixes by 2^k length prefixes iteratively in O(n log² n), consuming only O(n) memory without the 20x memory overhead of pointer-heavy suffix trees.
